description: message.rs line 376: expires_str.as_str() <= now.as_str() and space.rs line 582 (invite expiry check): same pattern. now_utc_string() produces YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SSZ with no fractional seconds. A client-supplied timestamp like 2025-06-01T12:00:00.000Z contains '.' (0x2E) which is less than 'Z' (0x5A), so a future millisecond-precision timestamp at the boundary second is incorrectly treated as already expired and rejected. Fix: parse both sides to a numeric epoch before comparing. Acceptance: a senderExpiresAt one second in the future with millisecond precision must not be rejected as expired.
title: Lexicographic ISO 8601 comparison fails with fractional-second timestamps
